evidence: src/interceptors/redact-values-in-response/redact-values-in-response.interceptor.ts: RedactValuesInResponseInterceptor.intercept checks the request's restricted access and then calls redactPaths({ object: data, paths: DEFAULT_REDACTED_PATHS }).
The access rules come from the shared hasReadRestrictedAccessPermission and isRestrictedView (@ghostfolio/common/permissions). They are not repeated locally.
The list of redacted paths comes from the shared DEFAULT_REDACTED_PATHS (@ghostfolio/common/config). It is not hard-coded in the module.

src/interceptors/redact-values-in-response/redact-values-in-response.module.ts: RedactValuesInResponseModule is an empty @Module({}). account.module.ts, activities.module.ts, portfolio.module.ts and user.module.ts import it, and their controllers use the interceptor.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module handles one thing: redacting sensitive values in HTTP responses when the request has restricted access. All the logic is in RedactValuesInResponseInterceptor. It relies on shared helpers for the access rules and the redaction instead of writing its own: hasReadRestrictedAccessPermission, isRestrictedView, redactPaths and DEFAULT_REDACTED_PATHS. So each rule is defined in one place and not repeated here. RedactValuesInResponseModule is an empty @Module({}). Other modules import it as a NestJS module, while controllers apply the interceptor class directly. That is normal for NestJS interceptors, so it doesn't bypass the module's own abstractions. The two files don't split into unrelated concerns.
